task.description:
WF-03 Step 2 GATE -- validate CODE-DESIGNER's design for ISS-0440 (lib/letflow/design/iss440-handoff-status-enforcement.md, commit dc7431b9). HARD GATE: PASS or FAIL. Apply your role's checklist plus the run-specific items below.

CONTEXT: this issue exists because SIX prior written-down mitigations for the same defect class all failed. The bar for this design is therefore unusually specific -- not 'is it reasonable' but 'does it eliminate the dependency on someone remembering'. Judge it against that.

1. THE CENTRAL CLAIM -- does the enforcement actually ride an UNAVOIDABLE action? The design names two, deliberately independent:
   A. Restricted --autofix riding mix letflow.check's unconditional CI invocation.
   B. A top-level status field READ inserted as a numbered clause INSIDE HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md 1.3's existing dispatch-time commit procedure, positioned before the commit step -- explicitly NOT a new skippable step.
   ORCH has independently verified the factual base for both: .github/workflows/ci.yml:126 is a single unconditional `run: mix letflow.check` with no `if:` and no `continue-on-error`, and mix.exs:91-108's alias does include letflow.lint_handoffs as a hard gate. So the FACTS hold. YOUR job is the harder question: does Mechanism B genuinely become unavoidable by being written as a clause inside an existing procedure, or is that still prose asking ORCH to remember -- just better-placed prose? This is the crux. ISS-0196/1.3 is cited as precedent on the grounds that it has held since adoption; TEST that precedent rather than accepting it -- is 1.3 actually complied with in practice across the corpus, and if so, is it because it is structurally enforced or because it happens to have been followed? If 1.3's own compliance rests on ORCH remembering, then Mechanism B inherits that weakness and the design must say so.

2. THE AUTOFIX REFUSAL. Verify the design restricts autofix to {PASS, COMPLETE, DONE} -> COMPLETED and REFUSES on FAIL and anything else, with the refusal being loud (non-zero exit, file untouched, named reason) rather than silent. Confirm the design cannot, under any path it specifies, convert a genuinely FAILED handoff into COMPLETED. This is the one place where a design defect would be WORSE than the bug being fixed, because it would corrupt the pipeline's record of what actually happened. Also consider a case the diagnosis may not have: what does autofix do with a handoff whose status is null/missing entirely, or a non-string? ORCH's own corpus scan found exactly one such file today (a PENDING handoff with null result.status -- legitimate), so null handling is a real path, not hypothetical.

3. AC2 -- THE HOOK REJECTION. The design REJECTS the .githooks/pre-push option, arguing an unconfigured host has zero protection and that the only possible detector would itself run inside mix letflow.check, making it circular. Judge whether that reasoning is sound or whether it disposes of a viable option too quickly -- a pre-push hook that catches the error 10 minutes before CI does has real value even if CI is the backstop. The design records it as an optional future latency-only addition. Is that the right call, and does the design satisfy AC2 as written (the mechanism works on a fresh clone by another host)?

4. AC1 -- THE DEMONSTRATION PATH. The design specifies ELIXIR-DEV plants a bad status into a SCRATCH FIXTURE (never a real handoffs/ file). Verify this actually demonstrates AC1 ('catches a deliberately-introduced bad status BEFORE CI, demonstrated by a real run with actual output quoted'). Specifically: does testing against a scratch fixture rather than a real handoff file weaken the demonstration? The linter discovers files via handoff_files/0 -- if a scratch fixture lives outside handoffs/, does the linter even see it, and if not, how is the demonstration valid? This is a real mechanical question, not a nitpick; get a definite answer from the source.

5. SCOPE AND SAFETY. The design changes lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex, which is a HARD CI GATE for EVERY in-flight run on every host. A defect here breaks every other session's ability to merge. Confirm the design's changes are additive (a new --autofix flag path) and cannot alter the DEFAULT no-flag behaviour that CI depends on. Confirm it does not change @legal_statuses, the grandfathering lists, or any existing check's verdict.

6. AC3/AC4/AC5. Confirm the design preserves '0 new violations, 25 pre-existing grandfathered' (AC3); that it updates docs/anti-patterns.md to record occurrence 8 AND the structural fix, so the entry stops being an open recurrence log (AC4 -- note the diagnosis found EIGHT occurrences, not the seven the issue text says); and that the cost claim holds (AC5) -- the design asserts neither mechanism adds a new full-corpus lint call site, with Mechanism B being an in-memory field read rather than a linter invocation. Verify that is actually what the design specifies.

Read anything. Do not edit lib/ or test/. Complete the handoff with a clear PASS/FAIL and per-item verdicts; on PASS route to ELIXIR-DEV. Commit to branch feature/WF03-ISS0440-20260903.

result.summary: FAIL. Read lib/letflow/design/iss440-handoff-status-enforcement.md directly, plus lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex, docs/anti-patterns.md, .github/workflows/ci.yml, mix.exs, docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md sections 1.1-1.3, and docs/agents/ORCHESTRATOR.md. Two independent BLOCKERs; per-item verdicts below.  ITEM 1 (crux) -- Mechanism B is NOT structurally unavoidable in the sense claimed, and the design overstates it. Empirically tested rather than accepted the design's own claim that section 1.3 'has held since adoption': (a) main's history is squash-merged per GIT_MERGE.md step 8 (verified: git log --oneline -3 --merges shows only 'Merge pull request' commits; every feature branch is deleted after squash), which destroys the dispatch-vs-completion commit-count evidence on main entirely -- an 88.5%-single-commit figure first measured across 1901 handoff files on main is an artifact of squashing, not evidence of non-compliance, and is not being cited as such. (b) This run's OWN unsquashed branch (feature/WF03-ISS0440-20260903) DOES show the two-commit dispatch-then-complete pattern live: step-02-code-designer.json has dispatch commit 45ac032a (ORCH, PENDING) followed by completion commit dc7431b9 (CODE-DESIGNER) -- direct evidence 1.3 is being followed today. (c) docs/anti-patterns.md:1123 records exactly ONE historical violation of the section-1.3-class defect (the ISS-0117/ISS-0196 incident that caused 1.3 to be written), with no logged recurrence since. (d) BUT: section 1.3 itself is a manual git-add-and-commit act ORCH must remember to perform -- docs/agents/ORCHESTRATOR.md:23 states it as a MUST-list bullet pointing at HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md 1.3, which is prose ORCH reads and complies with, not code that enforces it. Nothing prevents ORCH from writing H(n+1) and committing without having performed the design's inserted status-field read at step 2 of section 3.2's annotated procedure -- the numbered-sequence framing ('There is no path through this procedure that reaches step 4 without having passed step 2') is not literally true; it is a claim about a procedure being written in one place, not about anything code-enforced. The design must state plainly that Mechanism B rests on the SAME class of reliability as section 1.3 itself (a single party's disciplined manual compliance with written procedure, with a good but not code-guaranteed track record) rather than implying it inherits Mechanism A's CI-gate-strength unavoidability. As written, section 3.2 reads as 'prose asking ORCH to remember, better-placed' -- exactly the failure mode ISSUE-FIXER's own discriminator (design doc section 0) was meant to rule out -- and the design does not name this limitation anywhere in sections 1.2-3.3. This is a BLOCKER: the design must add an explicit paragraph stating this limitation, or explain what makes Mechanism B categorically different from the six failed prior mitigations beyond 'it's ORCH, not the completing agent, and ORCH has a clean record so far' -- which is a much weaker claim than the design currently makes.  ITEM 2 -- No live path converts a genuinely FAILED handoff into COMPLETED; refusal contract (sections 2.2/2.3) is loud, non-zero-exit, named-file, named-reason, matching the worked examples' shape. However the design's factual premise for the null-status path is imprecise: a full corpus scan (1919 files discovered by handoff_files/0's own step*.* glob semantics, verified against the actual Path.wildcard pattern) for missing/null/non-string top-level status found ZERO such files today -- not one. The single null-status file the handoff's dispatch text points to (handoffs/WF02-REQ197-20260830/test-run-report.json) has NO status key at all under either reading, and more importantly is a different, non-schema document (report_id/agent/verdict fields, not the handoff schema) whose basename 'test-run-report.json' does NOT start with 'step' and so is never discovered by handoff_files/0 in the first place -- confirmed directly via mix run against the live Path.wildcard call. The dispatch's premise conflated this with result.status (a different, legitimately free-form field) and misidentified the file. Per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md 1.1, a handoff's factual premise is checkable and this one does not hold as stated. This does not change the verdict on the missing/non-string path itself: check_h1_status/2's existing second clause (lines 426-435, pre-existing in the codebase, unmodified by this design) already correctly classifies a missing or non-string status as an H1 violation, and the design's autofix_map (section 2.2) correctly leaves it out of the {PASS,COMPLETE,DONE}->COMPLETED map, so it falls to the refuse-path by construction. Not a second BLOCKER on its own, but must be corrected on rework since a precision failure in the design's own evidence undermines confidence in the rest of its factual claims.  ITEM 4 -- FAIL, mechanical defect confirmed from source. handoff_files/0 (lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex:279) is defined as handoff_files(dir default @handoffs_dir), but run/1 (the actual mix letflow.lint_handoffs entry point, line 234) calls it as handoff_files() -- ZERO arguments, always resolving to the hardcoded 'handoffs' directory. There is no CLI flag today, and this design's section 2.1 scope is narrowly 'run/1 inspects args for --autofix' -- it adds no --dir-style override or any other mechanism for run/1 to discover files outside handoffs/. Verified directly: Python fnmatch and a live mix run against the actual Path.wildcard handoffs-star-star-slash-step pattern both confirm a file outside handoffs/ (e.g. scratch/ or test/fixtures/, exactly what section 5 step 1 specifies) is invisible to a mix letflow.lint_handoffs invocation. So section 5's demonstration steps 2-3 ('Run mix letflow.lint_handoffs [--autofix] against a fixture set including that file') cannot work as literally specified -- there is no such thing as 'a fixture set including' an out-of-handoffs/ file from run/1's perspective. The only way to make this demonstration real today is either (a) call handoff_files/1 and lint_file/2 directly in an ExUnit test with a custom dir argument, which is a materially different and weaker demonstration than 'a real run' with 'actual output quoted' (existing precedent: test/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs_test.exs already does exactly this for H6, at LintHandoffs.handoff_files(@fixture_dir), never via mix letflow.lint_handoffs from a shell), or (b) the design must add a directory-override mechanism to run/1 and specify it. The design currently does neither -- it asserts a CLI-level demonstration path that the source contradicts. This is exactly the kind of mechanical gap this gate exists to catch before reaching ELIXIR-DEV, per WF-02 Step 1b check 2a/2b (design element must be concrete, not silently assumed to work).  ITEM 5 -- Confirmed additive and safe. mix.exs:91-108's letflow.check alias is unchanged per the design's own section 6.3 and section 7 item 1 ('letflow.check alias in mix.exs is unchanged -- still calls plain letflow.lint_handoffs, no --autofix'); CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml:126, single unconditional run: mix letflow.check) is untouched by this design and continues calling the non-autofix path. run([])/run(['--check'])-shaped invocation is explicitly specified unchanged (section 2.1). @legal_statuses, the grandfathering lists, and H2-H6 are explicitly stated untouched (section 2.4: 'This design does not change how hard_new/hard_grandfathered are computed for any rule other than H1's autofixable subset'). Verified live: mix letflow.lint_handoffs (no flag, run this session) currently reports '0 new violations across 1919 handoff files (25 pre-existing grandfathered, traced to ISS-0190)' -- matching AC3's claimed baseline exactly, confirming today's default behavior is unaffected since ELIXIR-DEV has not yet touched the file. Zero H1 entries exist in @grandfathered today (grep-verified), matching section 2.5's claim that H1's grandfather list is empty.  ITEM 6 (AC3/AC4/AC5) -- AC3: satisfied by the closed mapping and refusal contract (section 2.2/2.3), consistent with the live '25 pre-existing grandfathered' baseline just measured, which the design does not touch. AC4: docs/anti-patterns.md instruction is honored in section 7 item 3 (no ninth tally line; a closing structural note instead) -- correctly deferred to DOC-UPDATER's Step 6, so nothing to fail here, though note the issue text's own 'SEVENTH occurrence' framing versus ISSUE-FIXER's count of eight is a pre-existing discrepancy the design did not introduce and correctly left to DOC-UPDATER. AC5: cost accounting (section 3.4) is consistent with the source -- Mechanism A adds no new call site (mix.exs alias unchanged, confirmed above) and Mechanism B is specified as an in-memory field read with no linter invocation, so the design's claim of avoiding the 74.7s contended full-corpus-lint cost is architecturally consistent with what it specifies, modulo Item 1's finding that the 'in-memory field read' is still a manual step ORCH must remember, not a structural guarantee.  VERDICT: FAIL. Two BLOCKERs (Item 1's overclaim, Item 4's broken demonstration path) plus one MINOR (Item 2's imprecise factual premise). Route back to CODE-DESIGNER with all three named below; this is not close enough to pass on the theory that ELIXIR-DEV could work around the gaps -- Item 4 in particular would send ELIXIR-DEV toward a demonstration that cannot succeed as specified, discovered only after implementation, which is exactly the late-discovery failure mode this gate exists to prevent.

issues.description: Item 1 (crux): design section 3.2 claims Mechanism B is unavoidable ('There is no path through this procedure that reaches step 4 without having passed step 2') because it is written as a numbered clause inside HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 1.3's existing procedure. This overclaims -- section 1.3 itself is manual compliance (ORCH remembering to git-add/commit at dispatch, per docs/agents/ORCHESTRATOR.md's MUST-list pointer), not code-enforced, so Mechanism B inherits that same reliability class rather than Mechanism A's CI-gate-strength guarantee. Empirically: main's squash-merge history (GIT_MERGE.md step 8) destroys direct corpus verification of section 1.3 compliance; this run's own unsquashed branch shows live compliance (dispatch commit 45ac032a then completion commit dc7431b9 on step-02-code-designer.json); docs/anti-patterns.md:1123 records exactly one historical violation (the incident that created 1.3) with no logged recurrence since. Rework: the design must state explicitly that Mechanism B rests on ORCH's disciplined manual compliance with written procedure -- the same class of mechanism as the six prior failed mitigations, just narrower in scope and with a better track record so far -- rather than presenting it as structurally unavoidable in the same sense as Mechanism A.

Item 4: design section 5's AC1 demonstration plan is mechanically invalid. run/1 (the mix letflow.lint_handoffs entry point, lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex:234) calls handoff_files() with zero arguments, which always resolves to the hardcoded 'handoffs' directory (line 279's default arg). A scratch/test-fixture file placed outside handoffs/ (as section 5 step 1 specifies, correctly, per File Placement Rules) is invisible to a real mix letflow.lint_handoffs/--autofix invocation -- verified directly via Path.wildcard semantics and a live mix run against the pattern. Section 5 steps 2-3 describe running the task 'against a fixture set including that file,' which is not achievable with the design's specified scope (only --autofix flag parsing is added; no directory-override mechanism is specified). Rework: either (a) add a directory-override mechanism to run/1's scope (e.g. a --dir flag or similar) and specify it in section 2, or (b) change section 5 to specify the demonstration as direct ExUnit calls to handoff_files/1 and lint_file/2 (or run_autofix/1) with a custom dir argument -- the existing precedent for exactly this pattern is test/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs_test.exs's H6 fixture test, LintHandoffs.handoff_files(@fixture_dir) -- rather than claiming a shell-level 'real run' against mix letflow.lint_handoffs that cannot see the fixture.

Item 2: design's stated factual premise ('ORCH's own corpus scan found exactly one such file today (a PENDING handoff with null result.status -- legitimate), so null handling is a real path, not hypothetical' -- from this handoff's own dispatch text, attributed to prior diagnosis) does not hold as stated. A full corpus scan (1919 files discovered by handoff_files/0's actual glob pattern) found ZERO files with missing/null/non-string TOP-LEVEL status today. The one null-valued field found in the corpus is result.status (a different, legitimately free-form field) on this run's own in-progress handoff, and the file the dispatch text points to (handoffs/WF02-REQ197-20260830/test-run-report.json) has no status key of either kind and is not even discovered by handoff_files/0 (its basename does not start with 'step', confirmed via mix run against the live Path.wildcard call) -- it is a different, non-schema report document. This does not change the substantive verdict (check_h1_status/2's existing missing/non-string clause, unmodified by this design, already correctly flags this case as a violation, and the design's autofix_map correctly excludes it from the safe-rewrite set), but the design's evidentiary basis should be corrected on rework since an imprecise factual claim undermines confidence elsewhere in the document.

result.next_action: Rework CODE-DESIGNER -- 2 BLOCKERs (Item 1 overclaim, Item 4 broken demonstration path) + 1 MINOR (Item 2 factual premise) named above, rework iteration 1 of 3
